purpose: Evidence-bounded comparison of cannabis cell production, plant extracellular vesicles, engineered bacterial cancer research, and untested combination hypotheses.
clinical_boundary: No combination here is a validated cancer therapy. Cannabis and cannabinoids are not established antineoplastic treatments in humans; none of these tracks is a clinical protocol, dosage recommendation, manufacturing instruction or patient treatment advice.

sources.title: Probiotic neoantigen delivery vectors for precision cancer immunotherapy
sources.limitation: Engineered probiotic vaccine preclinical work, not a cannabis-derived payload or a demonstrated human oncology therapy.

sources.title: Bioreactor-Based Suspension Cultures of Cannabis sativa for Enhanced Production of Anti-Inflammatory Cannabinoid Derivatives
sources.limitation: Demonstrates cell suspension production and anti-inflammatory assay findings, not selective tumor killing or delivery.

sources.title: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles as a novel tumor-targeting delivery system for cancer treatment
sources.limitation: Review of plant-derived vesicles broadly; does not establish a cannabis-specific vesicle cancer treatment.

sources.title: Cannabis and Cannabinoids in Adults With Cancer: ASCO Guideline
sources.limitation: Clinical recommendations about cannabis use in people with cancer; no cancer-directed cannabinoid use outside clinical trials.

tracks.title: Cannabis cell cultures as molecular factories
tracks.evidence_summary: Published bioreactor work reports scalable cultured cannabis biomass, putative cannabinoid derivatives, and anti-inflammatory assays.
tracks.not_demonstrated: No demonstrated tumor selectivity, anticancer clinical efficacy, or cancer-directed biomanufactured product.
tracks.research_question: Can reproducible chemical identity and batch purity be established for a specific molecule before studying biological effects?

tracks.title: Plant extracellular vesicles as delivery vehicles
tracks.system: Vesicles investigated across multiple non-cannabis plant species
tracks.evidence_summary: A 2025 review describes experimental interest in plant-derived vesicles for oncology drug delivery.
tracks.not_demonstrated: Cannabis-specific vesicle tumor targeting and efficacy are not established by this source.
tracks.research_question: Would any candidate vesicle show selective biodistribution and acceptable consistency compared with a standard carrier?

tracks.title: Engineered probiotic cancer-vaccine research
tracks.system: Engineered probiotic Escherichia coli neoantigen vectors
tracks.evidence_summary: Nature published preclinical engineered probiotic antigen-delivery research for cancer immunotherapy.
tracks.not_demonstrated: The cited system did not test cannabis compounds or prove that a cannabis-microbial combination treats patients.
tracks.research_question: What evidence demonstrates tumor-context specificity, immune effect, and systemic safety in published models?

tracks.title: Cannabis-derived molecule plus microbial carrier
tracks.system: Conceptual combination of purified plant-derived molecule and an experimental microbial delivery platform
tracks.evidence_summary: This combines ideas from separate literature streams; no direct combined efficacy evidence is asserted.
tracks.not_demonstrated: No published validation in these cited sources that this specific combination targets tumors, remains safe, or works in people.
tracks.research_question: Is there a compelling rationale beyond combining two interesting technologies, and what comparative evidence would falsify it?

tracks.title: Cannabis-derived vesicles carrying plant compounds
tracks.system: Hypothetical cannabis-cell vesicle source and cannabis-derived molecular cargo
tracks.evidence_summary: Plant-cell cultures and plant-derived vesicle delivery appear in separate lines of research; this cannabis-specific carrier concept is unverified.
tracks.not_demonstrated: No cannabis-vesicle cancer delivery, tumor selectivity, patient safety, or therapeutic efficacy shown by the cited sources.
tracks.research_question: Can cannabis-derived vesicles even be reproducibly characterized, and would they outperform established delivery controls?
readouts: Evidence that vesicles exist in characterized samples

tracks.title: Immune interference and clinical reality check
tracks.system: People with cancer receiving oncology care, especially immunotherapy
tracks.evidence_summary: ASCO recommends against cannabis or cannabinoids as cancer-directed treatment outside clinical trials and advises caution around immunotherapy.
tracks.not_demonstrated: In vitro cell effects are not a basis for human cancer treatment; the potential interaction profile is not resolved for proposed combinations.
tracks.research_question: Could immune-modulating effects undermine the intended antitumor immune response, and what human evidence exists?
